# Symphony + Claude Lane

> An installable agent skill that adds Claude Code as a specialist worker lane alongside Codex in an existing OpenAI Symphony + Linear workflow.

## What this is

A skill you install into an AI coding agent (Codex or Claude Code) to set up a mixed-lane orchestration system. Once installed, your agent can decide what work belongs to Claude versus Codex, create a durable routing profile in the target repo, and define visual verification, privacy, and closeout rules for the Claude lane.

## Who this is for

Developers and operators who already run Symphony + Linear with Codex workers and want to bring in Claude Code for work that benefits from visual judgment, browser verification, or design sensibility — UI implementation, frontend polish, product copy, and review work.

## Why two lanes?

Different AI agents have different strengths. Codex is fast and excels at bounded implementation in a sandbox. Claude Code has visual judgment, can verify frontend changes via Playwright, and handles design-sensitive work where tone and aesthetics matter. Running both against the same backlog — each claiming tickets that match its strengths — produces better output than either alone.

## Key concepts

- **Claude Lane**: A specialist worker lane for Claude Code, default-scoped to UI/UX, design, browser-verified work, product copy, and review.
- **Codex Lane**: The existing Symphony worker lane for implementation, refactors, infra, CI, types, and migrations.
- **Routing Profile**: A repo-local YAML file (`.orchestration/claude-lane.yaml`) that records what Claude owns, queue strategy, privacy rules, guardrails, and cleanup policy.
- **Visual Verification**: Playwright-first browser verification for frontend tickets before closeout.
- **Lane Labels**: Exact-match Linear labels that route tickets to Claude or Codex within the same project.

## Default workflow

Inspect repo -> confirm mixed-lane candidate -> confirm the base Symphony workflow has bootstrap assertions and a no-progress stop-loss -> ask adopter what Claude should own -> fall back to UI-first if unanswered -> create or update `.orchestration/claude-lane.yaml` including queue strategy, privacy rules, and retention policy -> prefer same-project label routing unless stronger separation is needed -> document lane contract -> use Playwright for visual verification -> apply safe closeout and cleanup rules

## Repo structure

- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/SKILL.md` — main skill definition
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/agents/openai.yaml` — skill UI metadata
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/references/setup.md` — prerequisites and candidate checks
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/references/routing.md` — routing defaults, extension questions, persisted profile contract
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/references/dispatch.md` — queue split, worker lifecycle, label routing
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/references/visual-verification.md` — Playwright-first browser verification guidance
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/references/closeout.md` — outcome blocks, In Review, retries, self-close rules
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/references/troubleshooting.md` — common mixed-lane failure modes
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/references/examples.md` — concrete ticket-routing examples
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/assets/claude-lane-profile.example.yaml` — example routing profile adopters copy into their repo
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/assets/claude-lane-guidance.snippet.md` — starter guidance for adopter repo orchestration docs
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/assets/worker-prompt.template.md` — reusable worker prompt template
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/assets/linear-outcome-block.example.md` — example structured closeout comments

## Install

```bash
npx skills add jvogan/symphony-claude-lane
```

Or copy `skills/symphony-claude-lane/` into your Codex skills directory or reference `SKILL.md` from Claude Code.

## Prerequisites

Requires an existing Symphony + Linear workflow. See [symphony-linear-starter](https://github.com/jvogan/symphony-linear-starter) to set one up.
